name: Power Loop
description: The most fundamental freestyle move — fly a full vertical circle, using motor power to carry the drone up and loop back down to the starting point.
steps: Start flying level at a moderate speed, with at least 15-20 meters of clear space above you
Push throttle up while pushing pitch forward (nose down) to start climbing into an arc
Hold throttle steady through the whole loop, adjusting pitch to shape the circle you want
At the top of the loop, ease off throttle slightly so you don't overshoot past where you meant to go
Continue down until you're back at your original altitude, then steady the throttle again
tips: Practice in wide open space first — never practice near people or obstacles
Start with big loops, then gradually tighten them once your throttle control is steady
If you get PID oscillation while climbing steeply (high-throttle oscillation), check the ConfigDoctor page alongside this
commonMistakes: Uneven throttle input makes the loop lopsided instead of round
Too much throttle at the start sends you higher than intended

name: Split-S
description: Fly up into a half-loop then flip inverted, descending in the opposite direction from where you started. Used to reverse direction quickly without turning.
steps: Fly level, then pitch up to start climbing into a half-loop (like the first half of a Power Loop)
At the inverted point (upside down), hold throttle steady and let the nose fall through along the same line
Continue pitching until the drone returns to level flight — now facing the opposite direction from when you started
tips: This builds directly on the Power Loop — once that's steady, Split-S isn't a big leap
Commonly used when you're approaching an obstacle and need to reverse direction immediately
commonMistakes: Letting off throttle while inverted causes you to lose altitude too fast to make your intended line
Not accounting for the altitude lost over the whole maneuver — easy to hit the ground/an obstacle if practicing in tight spaces

name: Barrel Roll
description: A full 360° rotation around the roll axis (front-to-back axis) while still flying forward in the same direction.
steps: Fly level at a constant speed with reasonable open space to the side
Hold the roll stick to one side until you complete a full rotation
Keep throttle steady through the whole roll so you don't lose much altitude
tips: If you're just starting out, practice at a lower roll rate first — it's easier to time the stop precisely
Practice both directions (left/right) until you're equally comfortable with each, not just your favored side
commonMistakes: Letting off throttle mid-roll causes altitude loss and throws off your heading
Releasing the roll stick before completing the full rotation leaves the move looking stuck halfway

name: Power Dive
description: Dive from altitude at speed, then pull up before reaching the ground. Used to build speed and change altitude quickly.
steps: Climb to a safe altitude first (noticeably higher than you think you'll actually need)
Pitch the nose down steeply, letting gravity help build speed — you can ease off throttle somewhat
Judge the distance carefully before your intended low point, then pull pitch up while adding throttle to pull out
tips: Always practice pulling out higher than you think you need to, especially the first few times at a new location
Watch out for propwash on the hard pull-out after a fast dive — if the drone shakes on pull-out, check D-term/filter settings on the ConfigDoctor page
commonMistakes: Pulling out too late because the accumulated speed was misjudged
Pitching down too steeply, making it hard to control direction close to the ground

name: Ground Skimming
description: Fly low, following the terrain's contours (rising and falling over low hills/obstacles). Prioritizes throttle precision over speed.
steps: Choose a route you can see clearly ahead of time, with no obstacles hidden from the FPV camera's angle
Fly low while holding a constant distance from the ground, adjusting throttle to follow the terrain's rise and fall
Fly slower than normal level flight, to leave yourself reaction time for obstacles that appear
tips: Start practicing higher off the ground than you actually intend to fly, then lower it gradually as you gain confidence
Light and shadow through the FPV camera can easily throw off your height judgment, especially in harsh sunlight
commonMistakes: Fixating on one point too long instead of scanning ahead for upcoming obstacles
Flying faster than your skill level allows, leaving insufficient reaction time

name: Wall Ride
description: Fly parallel alongside a steep wall or vertical surface, banking the drone slightly toward the wall for the whole pass.
steps: Approach the wall at a shallow angle (not head-on), holding a steady speed
Roll the drone to bank slightly toward the wall, so your flight line runs parallel to the surface
Hold the bank angle and distance from the wall steady for the whole pass
Before the wall ends, gradually roll back to level flight
tips: Practice judging distance from a wall in open space first (simulate the distance using something else you won't damage if you hit it) before trying a real wall
Consistent speed matters more than high speed here — this move is about steadiness, not speed
commonMistakes: Getting too close to the wall, leaving no margin to correct if you misjudge the distance
Rolling too far so your flight line angles into the wall instead of staying parallel

name: Matty Flip
description: A combo move that blends pitch and roll input at the same time, rotating the drone along a diagonal axis instead of a single roll or loop axis.
steps: Start flying level at moderate speed with reasonable clear space in all directions (this move uses more 3D space than a single-axis move)
Push pitch and roll together in roughly equal proportion, so the rotation follows a diagonal line
Hold throttle steady through the rotation, adjusting for the altitude lost during the move
Release both sticks back to center together once you've completed the rotation you wanted
tips: Get comfortable with Power Loop and Barrel Roll separately first, then work up to blending both axes at once
Start by practicing with a steady count/timing before attempting it as part of full freestyle flow
commonMistakes: Uneven pitch/roll proportion throws the rotation off the intended diagonal line
Releasing the two axes' sticks at different times makes the move look jerky at the end

name: Stall Turn (Hammerhead)
description: Climb straight up until speed is nearly gone, then yaw around to face the opposite direction at the top before diving back down.
steps: Climb straight up steeply on high throttle, letting speed bleed off gradually to gravity
As speed nears zero at the top, apply hard yaw input to spin the nose around to face the opposite direction
Once facing the new direction, let the drone dive straight down, then pull back up into level flight
tips: The yaw input only works once speed is nearly zero — timed too early, the drone won't finish the turn or will lose stability
Learn your own build's "speed-out point" first — every build climbs to a different height/speed before running out
commonMistakes: Yawing before speed has actually bled off causes the drone to lose stability mid-air
Not climbing straight enough vertically throws off the direction of the dive back down
